bmo_core_1809151.summary: The case tests whether an agent can drive an enterprise Kerberos-proxy iframe-auth regression from opening report → mozregression bisection → private HTTP log → the falsified "disable X-Frame-Options on your proxy" detour → identifying bug 1629307's XFO auth-suppression as the regressor → backout + reporter verification. The graph is a faithful rendering of the thread: comment provenance is exact (e3=c9–c11, e5=c23–c24), the bisection answer carries only raw mozregression output and never names bug 1629307, the engineer-only readings of the private log are correctly quarantined in info_inferred_by_engineer/inference_hint rather than required_info, the one blind path is a genuinely rejected proposal, and the root cause and satisfaction conditions match the engineer's own analysis in c9. Only three low-severity fidelity/labelling nits remain; none inverts scoring.
bmo_core_1809151.strengths: Blind-path labelling is correct and is the hardest thing to get right here: e3 ("disable X-Frame-Options on the corporate proxy") is exactly the proposal participant3 made in c10 ("If this is the case you could try disabling it as temporary fix") and that the reporter falsified in c11 ("I found no option to disable any X-Frame-Options. We do not manipulate any content of the website with the proxy"), while the move that actually fixed the bug — backing out 1629307 (c12 "Backout the regressing patch...", landed c22, confirmed c24) — is correctly is_known_blind_path=false. The measurement-class handling is exemplary: the mozregression edge (e1) and the HTTP-log edge (e2) are clarification_only, and e1's user_answer reproduces only the raw build/changeset/pushlog block from c2 without naming bug 1629307 — the mapping to 1629307 is explicitly deferred to info_inferred_by_engineer plus an edge comment, avoiding the dominant answer-key leak. Verification timing follows rule 4d: the Nightly retest sits terminal-side (e5) with fix-agnostic question patterns ("retest in today's Nightly and tell me what you see"), and its user_answer is verbatim c24. The root cause in satisfaction_conditions matches participant3's own c9 analysis (1629307 suppressed auth prompts for iframe responses that look XFO/CSP-blocked; here the XFO: deny came from the unauthenticated proxy response) and is corroborated by the later WIP attachment "disable XFO check for proxy auth". Denoise is clean: none of the substantial uplift/beta/release-note traffic (c13–c22, c25–c29) leaked into edges, required_elements, or satisfaction conditions; the 109.0.1 mention lives only in concrete_example as factual record. All required_info ids are gettable (start-node seeds plus the e1/e2 clarifications), the Task body is pure opening report with no later knowledge, the opening screenshot att9311319 genuinely shows the golem.de page with two "Proxy-Server verweigert die Verbindung" iframe panels and is hooked to N0 only, and persona_hint matches the reporter's behaviour including his habit of asking permission before retesting.

The page is now loading without any issues again!" — the reporter never characterises the build as "containing the fix"; SEMANTIC RULE 2 in src/graph_bench/pipeline/prompts.py says the terminal node states the observable end state, never engineering status.
confirmed_findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as the user's observation, e.g. "In today's Nightly the page loads completely again — the embedded iframe content comes through the corporate proxy without the refusal error."
confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: The rule citation checks out verbatim in prompts.py rule 2: "Aftermath nodes state the post-attempt OBSERVATION ...; the terminal node states the observable end state, never release management or engineering status." N_terminal.symptoms_visible[0] reads "Pages and their embedded iframe content load normally through the Kerberos-authenticated corporate proxy in Firefox builds containing the fix." The trailing clause characterises the build by its patch content — something the reporter cannot observe and never said; his words at c24 are "I can confirm, the issue is resolved in the nightly build from today. The page is now loading without any issues again!" The sentence is also third-person/generalised rather than the first-person voice rule 2 asks for. Mitigating: this is a terminal node, so there is no leak risk (the agent has already proposed the fix by then), the clause is a scoping qualifier rather than true release-management status (no uplift/relnote/version chatter, which rule 4c targets), and nothing machine-validated depends on it. Real but cosmetic — hence low, matching the reviewer's own severity rather than anything higher.

refuted_claims.claim: N3's symptoms_visible is a procedural question rather than an observable state, and it contradicts the node's own label and system-state assertion that the fixed build is already installed.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The cited defect class is not present: SEMANTIC RULE 2 forbids "diagnoses, causes, advice, or verdicts on an approach" in symptoms_visible, and N3's text contains none of those. It is c23 verbatim in the reporter's first-person voice ("Does the last post from Sebastian means that I can test if the problem is gone in the latest nightly build?") plus a plain state statement, "I haven't retested the affected page yet" — which IS the observable post-action, pre-verification state the fix-then-verify shape wants, and satisfies rule 2's first-person requirement. The claimed contradiction with the label is also weak: the opening body already says "Even in the beta and nightly the problem persists", so the reporter was running Nightly, and c24 arrives 21 minutes after c23 confirming "the issue is resolved in the nightly build from today" — installation of a build containing the backout demonstrably happened in that gap. S2 on N3 follows rule 1 ("system_state_id changes on EVERY persistent change to the user's system — each version installed") and rule 4d, which requires the retest of a build already containing the landed fix to sit terminal-side, i.e. exactly the e4-solution → N3(S2) → e5-verification → N_terminal shape the graph uses (see the e4 comment: "Reshaped per round-3 audit to the fix-then-verify pattern"). The reviewer's own proposed fix is semantically near-identical to what is already there ("I have not retested the affected page yet"), which marks this as a wording preference, not a defect.

refuted_claims.claim: The header-origin fact is graded L2_inferable although it is proxy-internal knowledge only the reporter holds and it was surfaced solely because the handler asked for it, which should make it L3_specific.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The reviewer's reading of the level rule proves too much. prompts.py rule 1 defines "L2 = inferable from evidence already surfaced; L3 = must be asked for or measured", and the sentence the reviewer quotes is specifically about "A fact visible in an artifact but only surfaced after a handler told the reporter to go check" — an artifact-inspection case, which this is not (the reporter checked nothing; he answered from his own knowledge of his proxy). If merely being asked forced L3, then every clarification would be L3 and the schema's L1_basic/L2_inferable options on Clarification would be dead letters. On the substance, the thread shows the core claim WAS inferable from already-surfaced evidence, and by the handler himself, before he asked: c9 (participant3) "AFAIU the header `X-Frame-Options` is added by the proxy and not by the site as it would deny loading the page even before our fix for Bug 1629307 was delivered", and c10 "we strongly suspect that the header `X-Frame-Options: deny` was added by the proxy and not the original website" (backed by his own devtools check of golem.de). That is textbook L2. Only the NTLM-fallback rationale in c11 is reporter-only knowledge, which is a partial argument for L3 but not a clear one. The cited defect_class (measurement_class_violation) is also wrong — rule 4 concerns edge typing of handler-initiated measurements, and this edge's typing is not challenged. Finally the reviewer concedes no required_info references the id, so the grading is inert either way. Not confirmable as a defect; default to refute.

gh_curl_curl_10936.summary: The case tests a long-running, non-reproducible use-after-free: nghttp2's on_stream_close() firing long after curl completed a timed-out transfer and the app closed the easy handle, because the stream user-data pointer was never cleared before RST_STREAM. The graph is a faithful answer key: both blind paths (upgrade to 8.2.x, upgrade to unpatched 8.5.0) were genuinely falsified in-thread by real retests, the two patch-validation tests are correctly modeled as clarification (measurement-class) edges rather than solutions, the multi-user merge is declared on every affected edge, and the root cause and fix commit match what participant3/participant6/participant1 actually established and merged. The only issues found are a blind-path intent whose wording ("curl 8.2.0 or newer") overlaps the correct fix recommendation, a small self-contradiction in the Task body, and a cosmetic reordering of when the crash-dump evidence appears.
gh_curl_curl_10936.strengths:
Blind-path discipline is correct, which is the usual failure mode. e1 (upgrade to curl 8.2.x) and e2 (upgrade to unpatched 8.5.0 per #12356) are the only blind edges, and both were genuinely tried and falsified in-thread — reporter 2023-08-18 "Still see this with cURL 8.2.1 and nghttp2 1.55.1, reverting cURL to 7.86.0 works around the issue", and reporter 2023-12-19 "curl 8.5.0 in combination with nghttp2 1.58.0 still crashes for me" (participant6 independently: "No, the issue still exists"). Nothing that actually worked is tagged blind.

Measurement-class handling is right: both patch trials on e4 — participant3's suggested one-liner nghttp2_session_set_stream_user_data(..., NULL) before nghttp2_submit_rst_stream(), and the reporter's 8.5.0+#12562 build — are modeled as clarification_only edges with the system_state_id held at S1, and their results are placed in user_answer, not in start info_state or volunteered_info, so the agent must ask for them. The reported numbers are verbatim faithful ("after 16 hours there's no single crash (usually it will have 6~7)"; "running for 2 days, a bit limited amount of testing").

Root cause and fix match the thread exactly: participant3's PR #12562 was "some small changes in clearing stream user data and checks on the seen user data in on_stream_close", merged by participant1 as 35380273b9311cf0741e386284310fa7ca4d005e; participant6's closing summary ("nghttp2 requires the user to take care of the user data before cancelling ... curl made some mistake so the user data is not correctly cleared") is what satisfaction_conditions[0] encodes.

The release-train discussion (reporter: "not merged and released with version 8.5.0, you need to cherry pick..."; participant1: "Scheduled to ship on January 31, 2024") is explicitly excluded from scoring in the e5 comment, avoiding a logistics gate. The multi-user merge (reporter, participant2, participant5, participant6) is declared on e2, e3, and e4. The Task body carries no post-filing knowledge. satisfaction_conditions cover all four required dimensions including the prohibition on the two falsified upgrades and a verification-under-load requirement. persona_hint ("initially lacks ... deep HTTP/2 internals knowledge") matches participant6's "I have almost zero HTTP2 knowledge before solving this bug" while still fitting the reporter's willingness to cherry-pick and run long field tests.

confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: The textual basis checks out verbatim. Thread c5 (participant1, 2023-07-24): "It would make a lot of sense to first test this problem with curl 8.2.0 or current git"; falsified by c15 (reporter, 2023-08-18): "Still see this with cURL 8.2.1 and nghttp2 1.55.1, reverting cURL to 7.86.0 works around the issue." c49/c50 confirm the real fix ships in 8.6.0 via commit 35380273. So e1.solution.intent's "curl 8.2.0 or newer" literally covers the correct release, and MATCH_EDGE_PROMPT / JUDGE_TURN_PROMPT (src/graph_bench/user_simulator/prompts.py) show intent text is what the online matcher scores against ("exact": the turn clearly satisfies one edge's intent), so a bare "upgrade to a newer curl" can be routed onto a scored dead end. BUT the reviewer's framing and severity are inflated: (a) the label is NOT mislabeled -- the attempt was genuinely tried and falsified, so is_known_blind_path=true is correct under the contract; the real defect is paraphrase drift in one intent sentence; (b) the scoring surfaces are already correctly scoped -- required_elements_for_full_match is "recommends_updating_to_curl_8_2_or_current_git", concrete_example says "curl 8.2.0 or current git", satisfaction_conditions #4 prohibits only "upgrading to curl 8.2.1 or to unpatched curl 8.5.0", and the offline matcher (matching.py) decides exact/partial on approach_keywords, not intent; (c) e6/e5 carry a far more specific intent (root cause + commit 35380273) that any genuinely correct answer matches better. gh_etcd-io_etcd_20418.summary: The case is the etcd "stale reads caused by process pausing" Antithesis linearizability failure, whose real answer key is: a follower reuses the same ReadIndex RequestCtx/request-id across retries to the same leader, so a delayed HeartbeatResp for that context flushes raft's readOnly queue and falsely confirms a newer queued read (fixed by PR 21399, generating a fresh request id per retry, verified by 0/4 fault-injection runs and 5 consecutive clean periodic CI runs). The graph is largely faithful: the blind path (leadership/select-race guess, commit ad284ef) is correctly marked as falsified because 1 of 3 runs on the patched branch reproduced the failure and the reporter himself called it "early bad guess"; the measurement edges (instrumented traces, fault-injection runs) are correctly typed as clarifications; the diagnostic-to-fix chain, image assignments and satisfaction conditions all match the thread. Two fidelity issues remain: the opening rev-3 vs rev-155 evidence is chained into the ReadIndex root cause although the thread attributed it to a different (snapshot-restore / current-rev:1) bug, and the fault-definition/timestamp-trust answers are positioned before the blind-path attempt although they only arrived after it.
gh_etcd-io_etcd_20418.strengths: The #1 failure mode is avoided: e3 (leadership-change/select-race patch, commit ad284ef) is correctly marked is_known_blind_path=true and lands on aftermath node N2_x whose symptoms match comment 23 verbatim in substance ("Out of 3 runs, the last one got a reproduction on branch with the fix"), corroborated by the reporter's own retraction in comment 26 ("Right, it was early bad guess"), and satisfaction condition 4 explicitly bars presenting it as the resolution. Measurement-class handling is exactly right: the instrumented raft/readOnly logging runs (e4) and the fresh-ID patch + periodic CI campaign (e5) are clarification edges whose answers report only run counts, raw IDs and queue events, with the causal conclusion deliberately parked in info_inferred_by_engineer + a well-written inference_hint. Clarification answers are quantitatively faithful to the logs (23.731 Txn proposed-index 11 / 24.193 Range start / 24.870 ReadIndex 7179191402480470886 / 25.817 index 10; retries at 17.225 and 17.728 reusing ID 3744633826720154659, new ID 3744633826720154677 after leader change; 2/3 unfixed runs vs 0/4 with 05c97884 and 5 consecutive CI passes), including the reporter's own 90ms→460ms self-correction. Image assignments all match their source comments (img0 opening, img2 to the c11 visualization edge, img3 to the reproduction-on-fixed-branch aftermath node, img5/img6 to the periodic/CI verification edge). The multi-user fold (participant1's artifact analysis, participant2's Antithesis fault semantics) is declared in the e1 and e2 edge comments, the Task body carries no later-thread knowledge, and the required_elements_for_full_match stay technical — notably the thread's long backport/cherry-pick/release tail (comments 50-56) was correctly excluded rather than encoded as a logistics gate.

That's why we saw that `Revision is 3` instead of 155 (the event was from etcd1)". Nobody rebutted this. All later diagnostic work (comments 8-11, 28, 31) uses entirely different Antithesis runs, and the merged fix PR 21399 is never connected back to the key26 rev-3/155 artifacts.
confirmed_findings.suggested_fix: Either drop same_key_operation_observed_at_revisions_3_and_155 from e6.solution.required_info.L2 (keep it as opening-context clarification only), or add an edge comment on e1 noting that this particular artifact was later attributed to a separate snapshot-restore issue and that the scored chain continues from the Feb reproduction runs.
confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: The factual base of the finding checks out. c0 (participant1, 2025-07-29) is the sole source of the key26/rev-3-vs-155 artifact, and it is faithfully rendered as the e1 clarification. c30 (participant3, 2026-02-27T19:56) reads the SAME July report (commit 472662fe) and traces etcd1's 'received and saved database snapshot' -> 'applied incoming Raft snapshot' -> 'kvstore restored, current-rev:1' and concludes '...it looks like related to this one - .../issues/20271 ... That's why we saw that `Revision is 3` instead of 155 (the event was from etcd1)'. I grepped the whole thread: the strings '155', 'key26', 'current-rev' and '20271' occur ONLY in c0 and c30. Nobody rebuts c30, and every subsequent diagnostic step (c11 Feb-24 run, c28 Feb-27 run, c31 Gemini trace, c32 run tallies) uses different Antithesis runs; PR 21399 is never tied back to key26. So making same_key_operation_observed_at_revisions_3_and_155 a hard L2 required_info of the final ReadIndex-reuse solution asserts a dependency the thread's own last word on that artifact contradicts. BUT the reviewer's severity and defect class are both inflated: (a) the graph's root cause is CORRECT (ReadIndex RequestCtx reuse), so 'wrong_root_cause' is the wrong label; (b) satisfaction_conditions #2 grounds the diagnosis in 'the ordered write/read evidence and the instrumented trace' and does NOT mention rev 3/155, so nothing in the scored rubric rests on it; (c) N1.symptoms_visible is a legitimate user-observable statement of the opening failure and e1 is a legitimate first clarification; (d) c30 is itself hedged ('it looks like related to this one') and unconfirmed. The practical harm is confined to one of eight required_info entries on e6, and the reviewer's own proposed fix (an edge comment on e1, or demoting it to opening context) is proportionate.

refuted_claims.why_refuted: The chronology the reviewer quotes is accurate but does not support the defect. Three independent reasons. (1) The gating info was already in the reporter's hands before the blind guess. e3.solution.required_info.L3 is exactly ['failure_run_included_container_pause_and_network_slowdown', 'read_request_later_received_index_10'] -- and BOTH come from c11 (reporter, 2026-02-24T10:03), a full day and a half before the c19 blind guess. c11's pasted log contains the fault_injector lines for pause/partition-Slowed/clog-Jammed/throttle plus the containers_meta pause/unpause events and the '25.817 ... received ReadIndex response ... index 10' line, and the reporter's own prose says 'Logs also include failures injected by Anththesis. Looks like we have combination of network partition and container pausing.' So the blind path IS reachable with the evidence the reporter actually had; c24 only added descriptive detail about what each fault does. (2) antithesis_log_timestamps_have_trusted_global_order is not in e3.required_info at all -- it sits only in N2.info_state -- so its placement gates nothing on the blind path, and the reviewer's framing that it is 'consumed as a prerequisite of e3' is simply wrong. Moreover the reporter was already operating on that assumption at c15/c17 ('It does indicate problem because the read started after the previous write has commited'), before the guess. (3) Under the semantic contract an edge is one assistant turn -- an ASK -- and the user_answer records what the user side eventually said. Both asks (c17 18:21 and c18 18:27) genuinely precede the c19 23:47 guess; only participant2's async reply lagged 28 hours. The graph declares the multi-user fold on e1 ('Contributors investigating the same failure are folded into one simulated user side'), and folding out an async participant's reply latency is precisely what that merge normalizes. Nothing in the contract requires canonical-path ordering to mirror wall-clock arrival of answers; the ordering constraints are info monotonicity and system-state constancy, both of which hold here (S1 throughout, containment satisfied).

gh_expo_expo_24172.summary: The case tests whether an agent can push past a plausible-but-wrong surface reading (content:// URIs are unsupported) and a rejected community fix (whatwg-fetch downgrade) to the real chain: reproduce on an affected Android 13 environment, notice that a package-only upgrade to expo-image-picker 14.5.0 did not help, and conclude that the local build was shipping stale expo-image-loader native code, fixed by a from-scratch build. The graph is a faithful and unusually well-constructed rendering of that chain — blind-path labeling, measurement-class edges, gettability and engineer-inference separation are all correct. The defects are one over-reach in the scored fix (making expo-image-manipulator alignment mandatory although the maintainer explicitly denied it and it was only confirmed for a different user) and two mild leaks of later-thread details into the opening body and the first retest answer. None inverts the answer key.
gh_expo_expo_24172.strengths: Blind-path handling is correct and is the hardest part of this case: e1 tags exactly the one falsified suggestion in the thread (whatwg-fetch 3.6.2 downgrade, c1 → reporter's c2 "are you sure? I have 3.6.2" with yarn output → c4 "that's not the error I'm getting"), and its aftermath node N1_x states the post-attempt observation without diagnosis. Measurement-class discipline is exemplary: the 14.5.0 upgrade-and-ship retest (e3), the emulator reproduction plus yarn why plus Sentry stack (e4), and the clean EAS build (e5) are all modeled as clarification_only with the result in user_answer, even though the EAS build doubles as a workaround — only the final clean-rebuild prescription (e6) changes system_state to S2. Every id in e6.required_info is granted upstream, so nothing is required-but-ungettable. The engineer-only content is properly quarantined: root_cause_old_image_loader_native_code and content_uri_exception_is_secondary_not_root_cause sit in info_inferred_by_engineer with an inference_hint that faithfully reproduces c20/c21 ("It's a permissions issue... causes a SecurityException from Glide", "The exception you see is the second one... The content uri isn't the problem") and c54 ("All photos that come back from the photo picker come as content Uris"). The multi-user folds are declared in edge comments for both participant4/participant5 (e3) and participant6 (e6). The e6 comment correctly notes that gradle-cache deletion was discussed (c72/c73) but never verified by the reporter, and scores the general clean rebuild instead of the specific rm -rf command. User answers I checked (e2, e3, e4, e5) are quoted faithfully against c8/c13, c36/c38, c43/c55/c57, and c71 respectively, and the persona_hint matches the reporter's actual behaviour (Sentry/analytics fluency plus "I have no idea what is an uri with content://").

refuted_claims.claim: The scored fix makes expo-image-manipulator/expo-image-loader dependency alignment a required part of the answer, but in this thread that theory was the reporter's own guess and the maintainer explicitly denied it, while the reporter's actual resolution was a from-scratch build (stale local native code), not dependency realignment.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The reviewer's quotes are accurate but the reading stops at c46. The maintainer's denial is falsified later in the SAME thread: c74 participant6 reports he had ALREADY 'upgrad[ed] media library and image picker and clear[ed] the gradle cache' and still failed; c75/c76 reporter says try expo-image-manipulator 11.5.0 + run `yarn why expo-image-loader`; c77 'That worked.' Clean rebuild alone was demonstrably insufficient there. c78 participant7 supplies the mechanism explicitly for a local build with caches cleared: the Android autolink list prints `expo-image-loader (4.3.0)` alongside `expo-image-manipulator (11.3.0)` and `expo-image-picker (14.5.0)` — i.e. a stale manipulator pins the native loader to 4.3 no matter which loader picker 14.5.0 vendors. So the reviewer's PROPOSED replacement requirement (picker 14.5.0 + clean from-scratch build, alignment optional) is precisely the configuration the thread shows still failing at c74 and c78. The answer key encodes the true root cause, not the maintainer's mid-thread opinion. Also, the reviewer overstates what the graph actually scores: required_elements_for_full_match[1] is the generic 'requires_fixed_expo_image_loader_4_4_compatible_dependencies' (not 'must name expo-image-manipulator'), satisfaction_conditions[2] phrases manipulator as an illustration ('any dependency such as expo-image-manipulator that leaves loader 4.3 selected'), and 'requires_clean_native_android_rebuild' is a separate co-equal element that already carries the reporter's own c71 EAS verification. The e6 comment further declares the multi-user fold. Note too that the reporter's own EAS success is confounded, not contrary evidence: at c45/c47 he said he was deploying with the latest expo-image-manipulator BEFORE the c70/c71 EAS build, so that build plausibly carried both the alignment and the clean rebuild — which is exactly why demanding both is the safest encoding.

refuted_claims.claim: The 14.5.0 retest answer already tells the agent the release was a LOCAL build, which is the decisive clue for the eventual root cause, but the reporter only disclosed his local-build workflow later, when the maintainer asked how he ships updates.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The ordering observation is right (c36/c38 mention only 'It look like it's still there', 19.44.0 and the changelog; `eas build -p android --local` surfaces at c49 answering c48), but the characterization fails on two counts. First, 'decisive' is not supported: participant2 KNEW the build was local from c49 (19:13 on 2023-09-06) and still needed the emulator reproduction, the APK, the dependency tree and a day of log analysis before landing on 'I suspect the native code is out of date' at c69 (2023-09-07T15:47). Knowing the build is local is a starting condition, not the answer. Second, the encoding is required for graph coherence, so removing the word would break gettability rather than fix a leak: e5's clarification question is literally 'verify whether the issue still occurs in a from-scratch EAS build rather than your local Gradle build', and the final solution's required_info L3 depends on image_picker_14_5_local_production_build_still_fails; if 'local' were never surfaced, the e5 measurement and the 'clean native rebuild' element would be un-grounded. A user's own standing build workflow is stable system context that a simulated user can truthfully state when describing how he shipped the retest — it is not investigative knowledge produced later. The residue is a ~7-comment forward shift of a self-known fact: fidelity drift at most, and the reviewer's alternative (add an explicit build-workflow clarification) is a refinement, not a defect correction.

gh_flutter_flutter_124205.summary: The case tests whether an agent can drive a long, noisy, multi-user Flutter-web keyboard-offset thread past two popular-but-falsified workarounds (Scaffold resizeToAvoidBottomInset=false, avoiding programmatic requestFocus) to the real cause — Flutter mobile-web not restoring viewport geometry across virtual-keyboard transitions, producing a shrunken height and a negative bottom view inset — fixed by PR 179581 / stable 3.38.6. The graph is highly faithful: both blind paths are genuinely falsified in-thread (c3/c25/c35/c78 for the Scaffold property; c55/c77 for the focus workaround), the clarification order mirrors the thread's actual order (physical devices c0-c1, HTML renderer c6-c7, MediaQuery logging c100, fixed-build retest c109-c110), the update-and-retest step is correctly modeled as a clarification rather than a solution, and the engineer-side PR-equivalence inference is kept out of hard required_info. Only two low-impact fidelity nits: the e5 answer relabels which state the "normal" 412x770/+312 log came from, and e1's attached images/comment are slightly mismatched with the answer text.
gh_flutter_flutter_124205.strengths: Blind-path labelling is exactly right on both branches and is the hardest thing to get right in this thread. e2 marks resizeToAvoidBottomInset=false blind with a required element scoped to "as complete fix", which is precisely what the thread falsified (reporter c3 "Already tried ("; participant13 c25 "The workaround didn't work for me... I set resizeToAvoidBottomInset: false for all of them but still have the issue"; participant20 c35; participant53 c78 "fixes this issue on iOS Apps, iOS Safari web, Android App but fails on Android web") — while the terminal solution and satisfaction condition 4 still correctly preserve it as a legitimate Android-web Scaffold setting, matching participant73's final confirmation (c110) that the fix works "provided that you disable the resizeToAvoidBottomInset for Android web in the scaffold". e4 likewise marks the requestFocus workaround (c52, confirmed by c53) blind on the strength of c55 ("that is why @participant36 workaround works at some degree but is not a reliable fix") and c77 ("im not using focus at all and it is still happening"). The clarification chain follows the thread's real order (c0/c1 physical devices, c6/c7 HTML renderer, c100 MediaQuery capture, c109-c110 fixed-build retest), and the fixed-build retest is correctly modeled as a clarification per the measurement-class rule rather than a solution edge. The root cause and satisfaction conditions track c101 ("Flutter not properly setting screen geometry after the virtual keyboard is dismissed") and c108 (identical to #175074, fixed in PR 179581, cherry-picked to stable 3.38.6), with the PR-equivalence step properly confined to info_inferred_by_engineer plus an inference_hint rather than hard required_info. The Task body carries no later-thread knowledge, N4 vs N_terminal cleanly separates "symptoms gone" from "resolved and verified", and the multi-user fold is declared on e1, e4, e6 and in persona_hint.

gh_flutter_flutter_140138.summary: The case tests a long, evidence-driven regression hunt: Flutter 3.16.x tooling dying with exit 3221225501 on pre-SSE4.1 x86-64 CPUs, ultimately root-caused to a hole in the Dart VM's JIT CPU-feature restriction that let a `roundsd` (SSE4.1) instruction be emitted, fixed in Dart 3.3.3 / Flutter 3.19.5. The graph is a faithful, well-shaped rendering of that chain: the single blind path (generic MSB8066 troubleshooting) really was tried and failed, the diagnostic ladder (version sweep → verbose logs → CPU models → bisect → floor.dart/--target-unknown-cpu → --trace-cpuid → 3.19.5 verification) matches the thread's actual order, every handler-initiated probe is a clarification edge, and the multi-user merges are declared. Two fidelity issues remain, neither of which inverts scoring: one clarification answer mischaracterizes where the verbose runs actually died, and one aftermath node carries an info id no edge into it grants.
gh_flutter_flutter_140138.strengths: The one blind edge is correctly labeled: comments[0] (participant1 links the MSB8066 Stack Overflow thread) followed by comments[1] ('I have tried the things mentioned under that thread but nothing worked for me') is a genuine in-thread falsification, and the aftermath node's symptoms describe the post-attempt state. Nothing that actually worked is tagged blind. The root cause in e7 and in satisfaction_conditions matches the thread exactly: participant10's explanation ('When JIT compiling, dart vm relies on cpu detection logic ... It looks like though there was a hole in how determined restrictions were applied'), participant11's `roundsd`/SSE4.1 identification, the fix CL 357218, Dart 3.3.3, and Flutter 3.19.5 (announced by participant12). Every handler-initiated probe is modeled as a clarification edge with the measured result as the answer -- the version sweep, the flutter run -v capture, the git bisects, floor.dart with and without --target-unknown-cpu, --trace-cpuid, and the 3.19.5 re-test -- and none of those results leak into the start node or volunteered_info. The bisect answer preserves both users' raw first-bad hashes (47ba59c from participant7, ee4208fd from participant9) without pre-resolving which roll mattered, and the mechanism ('SSE4.1 emitted despite the restriction') is correctly parked in info_inferred_by_engineer with an inference_hint rather than in hard required_info -- the gettability check on both solution edges comes back clean. The multi-user folding (participants 2/3/7/9 into one user side) is declared in the comments of e3, e4, e5 and e6, and the reporter's own CPU model is modeled as spontaneously volunteered on N2_x, exactly as in comments[3] ('I'm on a very old system that uses an AMD Phenom(tm) II X4 965 Processor'). The Task body is clean opening-report material with no later knowledge. The satisfaction_conditions correctly prohibit the thread's two dead ends (generic MSB8066 work and participant7's mixed path-separator theory, which participant5 dismissed with 'I don't think this is fatal') and refuse downgrading to 3.13.9 as a permanent fix, matching participant10's 'we only hotfix the latest version'; they also require verification on affected hardware, which the graph enforces structurally by gating the terminal behind N6 (participant9's 3.19.5/Dart 3.3.3 retest with 'ceil result: 1016!').

confirmed_findings.claim: at graph.edges[e3_N2_x__N3].clarifications[verbose_runs_die_when_dart_frontend_tool_executes].user_answer_in_this_oncall (and N3.symptoms_visible[0]): the answer states that all three verbose runs stop while the cached Dart executable is launching Flutter's frontend tooling, but the reporter's logs show the Android and Windows runs completing kernel_snapshot and printing 'build succeeded' before the nested flutter process died; only the web run stops at the frontend_server invocation.
confirmed_findings.verifier_reasoning: Independently confirmed against comments[9] (reporter, 2023-12-20, 86KB of flutter run -v). Android section (lines 339-358 of that comment): '[+17567 ms] [+18623 ms] kernel_snapshot: Complete' -> 'debug_android_application: Complete' -> 'build succeeded.' -> '> Task :app:compileFlutterBuildDebug FAILED' -> "Process 'command 'I:\soft\installed\flutter\flutter\bin\flutter.bat'' finished with non-zero exit value -1073741795". Windows section (lines 967-981) is identical in shape: 'kernel_snapshot: Complete' -> 'debug_bundle_windows_assets: Complete' -> 'build succeeded.' -> 'error MSB8066 ... exited with code 1'. Only the Web section (lines 1076-1092) truly ends at the dart.exe frontend_server invocation followed by '<- compile org-dartlang-app:/web_entrypoint.dart' with no further output. So the graph's 'get through setup and pub work, then stop while the cached Dart executable is launching Flutter's frontend tooling' misstates 2 of the 3 measurements: both native targets got through the whole Dart kernel compile and asset bundling. It also puts a characterization in the user's mouth that the thread only reaches later as engineer inference (comments[14], participant5 2024-01-03: 'during the re-entrant call from cmake to flutter assemble, the flutter tool is dying without a stacktrace'; comments[18] hypothesizing 'the frontendserver AOT snapshot'), which violates 'symptoms_visible = ONLY observable phenomena in the user's words' and 'user_answer states what the measurement showed'. Two partial defenses do NOT rescue it: (a) on Android/Windows the process that dies IS a cached-dart-run flutter tool (flutter.bat --verbose assemble), so the wording is loosely true of the sub-process identity; (b) the same answer does preserve 'Windows reports the MSBuild custom-build exit'. I also partly refute the reviewer's PROPOSED FIX: the claim that -1073741795 'is currently dropped' is wrong -- the Task body already states 'building for Windows fails through MSBuild with exit code -1073741795', and 3221225501 (in N0.info_state) is the same value unsigned. Scoring impact is limited (this info_id is required by e7 but the crash-location wording does not change the answer key or the SSE4.1 diagnosis), so medium, not high.

gh_flutter_flutter_140504.summary: The case tests whether an agent can drive a Flutter-web "shader compilation error" report all the way out of Flutter and into a Chromium ANGLE-on-Metal regression on Intel macOS, using browser-channel/architecture scoping, about:gpu + raw shader output, a network-JPEG format bisection, and a BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false probe, ending in a Chrome-update verification. The graph is largely faithful: the canonical chain, the root cause, the measurement-class handling of the dart-define probe, and the multi-user merge all match the thread, and the two blind branches (chrome://flags OOP canvas rasterization, Chrome Beta v123) correspond to real falsifications (c30/c26 and c70). Remaining problems are fidelity-level: the v123 blind edge is authored broadly enough ("update_browser") that it overlaps the correct "update Chrome to the corrected build" answer, and it is a version probe modeled as a system-changing solution while its target node keeps system_state S1. Nothing rises to a wrong root cause, ungettable required info, or a future-knowledge leak.
gh_flutter_flutter_140504.strengths: Root cause and terminal semantics are right and well grounded: e7's intent, satisfaction condition 1, and the terminal both name the Chromium ANGLE-on-Metal regression on Intel macOS rather than a Flutter shader, matching c17 ('a regression in Apple's Metal shader compiler in macOS 14'), c18 ('the shader which is failing to compile is not actually one coming from Flutter's copy of CanvasKit, but rather one being compiled by Skia inside the browser'), c60 ('somewhere between ANGLE and Metal deep inside Chromium') and c72 ('the ANGLE-Metal experiment has been disabled in Chrome on Intel Macs'). The 4d reshaping (fix proposed on pre-fix evidence at e7 → N6 fix-applied-but-unverified → e8 verification → terminal) correctly separates 'symptoms gone' from 'resolved and verified', and satisfaction condition 6 demands user verification, matching c76/c77/c78 and the reporter's close at c79. The measurement-class rule is applied correctly to the two probes that matter: the Flutter master channel test (e2, from c6/c7) and the --dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false build (e5, from c63/c64) are both clarification_only even though the latter doubles as a workaround, and e5's comment carries participant3's UI-thread-jank caveat from c65. The clarification answers are verbatim-faithful: the Chrome 121.0.6167.16 x86_64 / 2020 Intel MBP detail (c2/c5), the Stable-120 / Beta-121 / Canary-122 matrix (c12), the about:gpu workaround names and 'Canvas out-of-process rasterization: Disabled' (c14/c15), the CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL / INVALID_OPERATION lines and the uTextureSampler_0_S0 + ucircle_S1_c0 shader body (c23), and the JPG/JPEG-vs-PNG/WebP/GIF split (c45/c50/c52). Symptoms stay observational everywhere — N3 reports what the console printed without asserting a Metal/ANGLE cause, and the engineer-side conclusions live in info_inferred_by_engineer/inference_hint rather than hard required_info. gh_flutter_flutter_154241.summary: This case tests a long, noisy Flutter CameraX preview-rotation regression where three successive maintainer attempts (duplicate closure, the API-29 0.6.9 correction, the 0.6.12 rotation-logic removal) each failed or only partly worked before PR 8629 / 0.6.14 fixed it via preview rebuild-on-orientation plus SurfaceProducer.handlesCropAndRotation. The graph is technically faithful: the root cause, all three blind paths, the evidence chain and the image assignments match the thread, and the measurement-class rule is applied deliberately. The blocking problem is structural rather than semantic — the resolution chain hangs off the blind "remove the rotation logic" edge, so the benchmark's canonical (non-blind) path from N0 reaches no terminal at all, and an agent that obeys satisfaction_conditions #4 can never resolve the case. Two smaller reveal-ordering issues (start-node answer citing the not-yet-mentioned earlier Impeller fix; e7 handing over "0.6.14 works" before e8 scores recommending it) also degrade the answer key.
gh_flutter_flutter_154241.strengths: The hard parts of this very long (184-comment) thread are modeled correctly. (1) Root cause is exactly right: e8 and satisfaction_conditions state both halves of participant5's c161 conclusion — the preview was only a Texture so orientation-stream updates never rebuilt it, and API level was an unreliable proxy for whether the SurfaceProducer backend already handled crop/rotation (handlesCropAndRotation) — and correctly place these in info_inferred_by_engineer rather than hard required_info. (2) All three blind paths are genuinely falsified in the thread: the duplicate closure to #149294 (c1) rejected by the reporter with version+renderer evidence (c2); the PR 8256 rotation-logic removal that shipped in 0.6.12 and broke the previously-correct Pixel 7 (c100, c114, c115) while leaving Galaxy Tab wrong (c95); and the fixed RotatedBox(quarterTurns: 1) workaround (c140) retracted once the device is rotated (c142, c152). No accepted approach is mislabeled blind. (3) The measurement-class rule is applied and defended in comments: testing 0.6.9 (e4) and 0.6.14 (e7) are clarification edges, not solutions. (4) Every id in e5's and e8's required_info is grantable by an earlier clarification or the start node — no ungettable requirements. (5) Images are attached to the right evidence: img1/img2 (c15, stretched preview vs unstretched photo_view) on captured_photo_is_not_stretched_like_live_preview; img3-6 (c18, Pixel Tablet orientations) on the broader repro; img7-10 (c30, four-orientation test of the API-29 correction) on the remaining landscape cases; img11/img12 (c140) on the RotatedBox aftermath. (6) satisfaction_conditions correctly separate the live-preview defect from the separately-tracked rotated recorded-video issue (c68/c69) and require physical-device verification without a manual workaround (c182). (7) symptoms_visible stay observational throughout, the Task body carries no later-thread knowledge, and persona_hint matches a reporter who read the plugin source (c0) and ran targeted emulator images (c25).

The diagnostic spine (N0→N1→N1_x→N2→N3) is a faithful, well-ordered reconstruction of comments 0-39, and the single blind path is correctly grounded. The tail of the graph is where it breaks down: the terminal verification the graph puts in the user's mouth ("I applied Docker 28.0.1 … routing works again") was never given by any Tailscale-affected participant — it is lifted from the swag/rocky9 and Oracle Cloud sub-issues — and the answer key promotes 28.0.1 to "the durable fix" more strongly than the thread supports for this specific setup.
gh_moby_moby_49498.strengths: The #1 historical defect is handled correctly here: the only blind path (e2, moving Tailscale's ts-forward jump into DOCKER-USER) is exactly the attempt participant1 proposed in c6 and participant2 falsified in c7 ('only doing iptables -I DOCKER-USER -j ts-forward / iptables -D FORWARD -j ts-forward didnt help for me'), and participant1 later confirmed why it failed (c19: 'I misunderstood ... which I guess explains why just moving the ts-forward rule didn't help'). The aftermath node N1_x and satisfaction_conditions[3] enforce it properly. The measurement-class rule is applied correctly and non-obviously on e4: disabling stateful filtering is both a probe and a workaround, and the graph keeps it clarification_only with an explicit justifying comment. The clarification order matches the thread's real order (direct-IP + bridge config + iptables dumps at c1-c13, then the DOCKER-USER attempt at c6-c7, then the stateful-filtering question at c33 and the toggle result at c36/c39). The Task body is clean — it carries only the reporter's opening DNS theory and the 27.5.1 rollback, with no hint of iptables ordering or stateful filtering. satisfaction_conditions[0] correctly forces the agent off the DNS theory using the direct-IP evidence (c1, c3), and satisfaction_conditions[4] correctly forbids the DROP-rule deletion/chain-flushing workarounds circulated in c4/c10/c23, matching participant1's warning in c6. gh_ollama_ollama_6756.summary: The case tests whether an agent can resist the obvious "your VRAM prediction is off, reserve memory / drop layers" reading of an AMD segfault and instead drive to a version-boundary bisection that fingers an Ollama-side ROCm regression between 0.3.6 and 0.3.7, fixed in 0.3.14. The graph is a faithful and well-structured rendering of the thread: every node, clarification answer, and the one blind path are backed by specific comments, and no approach the thread accepted is tagged as a dead end. The two issues found are both about the final solution's confidence level rather than its direction: the graph asserts commit 0b03b9c's ROCm build change as the established cause (the thread only floated it as an unconfirmed guess, and the graph's own satisfaction_conditions say so), and the blind edge bundles a num_gpu reduction the reporter never actually reported trying. Neither inverts the scored diagnostic chain.
gh_ollama_ollama_6756.strengths: The graph tracks the thread's actual diagnostic arc closely and in the right order: c2/c3-c4 (no custom params + full runner log + Arch ROCm 6.0.2 + 32 GB RAM) -> c5-c12 (OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD escalated to 10 GB, still segfaults) -> c20 (self-downgrade to 0.3.6, `ollama ps` 21 GB / 100% GPU) -> c22/c34 (official build with bundled ROCm, same failure) -> c43/c44 (0.3.6 works, 0.3.7 segfaults) -> c46/c50 (environment matrix + 0.3.12 log) -> c53/c56 (0.3.14-rc0 verified). The only blind path (e2) is genuinely falsified in-thread, and the maintainer confirms the class is dead (c22, c46) — no accepted approach is mislabeled as blind. Numeric details in the clarification answers are exact against the raw logs: e1's "22.7 GiB available / 21.7 GiB required / 41 layers / --no-mmap" matches c3 verbatim, and e6's "22.7 GiB available / 20.1 GiB required / all 41 layers" matches c50 verbatim. e3 correctly types the 0.3.6 downgrade as a successful *temporary* workaround (is_known_blind_path=false, is_shortcut=true), a spot where LLM drafts routinely mislabel. The measurement-class rule is applied consistently and defensibly: the official-build test (e4), the 0.3.6-vs-0.3.7 boundary probe (e5), and the 0.3.14-rc0 verification (e7) are all clarification edges with the state change tracked separately in system_state_id. The multi-user fold of participant9's 0.3.7 confirmation is explicitly declared in e5's comment. The Task body is clean opening-report voice with no later knowledge, symptoms_visible are pure observations throughout, satisfaction_conditions cover root cause, evidence grounding, prohibition of both falsified moves, downgrade-as-workaround-only, and user verification, and the persona_hint matches the reporter's behaviour (c6 asks for docs on the env vars; c12 plainly reports the failed experiment).

refuted_claims.claim: The final solution states the 0.3.7 regression as being caused by "the ROCm runner build change associated with commit 0b03b9c" and makes identifying that build change a hard full-match requirement, but the thread only ever offered that commit as an unverified guess and never linked it to the 0.3.14 fix — this also directly contradicts the graph's own satisfaction_conditions[0].
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The graph's actual root cause is right and is exactly what the thread supports: c44 (participant9) 'Can confirm. ollama 3.6 works, 3.7 segfaults'; c53 (participant2) 'the main issue should be resolved in 0.3.14'; c56 reporter 'Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 works great!'. The hard grading slot required_elements_for_full_match[0] is the string 'identifies_regression_as_introduced_in_0.3.7_rocm_runner_build_change' — it never names or requires commit 0b03b9c, so the claim that commit identification is a hard full-match requirement is not supported by the cited text. The graph already quarantines the inference exactly as the contract demands: info_inferred_by_engineer = [rocm_runner_build_regression_introduced_in_037, main_regression_fixed_in_0314], and inference_hint states verbatim that 'Associating that boundary with the ROCm compile/build change restored by commit 0b03b9c ... is engineer-side inference from the repository history and maintainer comments'. Edge e5's comment repeats it ('mapping that boundary to commit 0b03b9c is engineer-side inference'). Characterizing the regression as an Ollama-side ROCm *build/runner* change is itself independently grounded, not free-floating: the official bundled-ROCm build reproduces it (c34), c45 reports deleting Ollama's own lib/rocm let 0.3.9 work when compiled from source, c31/c33 tie behavior to which ROCm libraries ship with the build, and 0b03b9c is a compile flag. The only genuine residue is prose in concrete_example ('after the ROCm runner build change associated with commit 0b03b9c') being less hedged than satisfaction_conditions[0], which permits the commit 'only as the maintainer's unconfirmed hypothesis' — a wording nit in an illustrative field, not a contradiction of the grading contract and not a wrong root cause. An edge is ONE assistant turn, and c5 (participant2) is a single turn proposing both options as one memory-prediction workaround: 'you can set `num_gpu` to a smaller value (try 40, 39, ...) or use the new env-var `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD` to reserve some VRAM so our algorithm calculates less layers to load' — the maintainer himself frames the overhead knob as the means of loading fewer layers, so 'reserve_vram' and 'reduce_gpu_layers' are one approach, not two. The falsification is real and doubly in-thread: (a) mechanically, the reporter's own test in c12 ('I've tried an overhead up to 10 GB but still wouldn't load the model') on a 24 GB card forces Ollama to offload substantially fewer than 41 layers — that IS the num_gpu reduction path, executed via the same code path; c36 confirms the mechanism ('Setting OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD ... to ludicrously high values (20 GB) ... the model would run effectively entirely on the CPU'); (b) at class level the maintainer explicitly falsified it in c22 ('this is not actually a memory prediction error') and c46 ('The fact that OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD doesn't seem to help implies it's not a simple over-allocation'), and participant3 in c13 ('if 10 GB overhead didn't let the model load, it sounds like something else is going on'). The graph does not overclaim what was measured: the aftermath node N1_x, its info id gpu_overhead_up_to_10gb_still_segfaults, the edge comment ('The reporter tested values from 1 GB through 10 GB on 0.3.10'), and satisfaction_conditions[2] ('GPU overhead up to 10 GB and the official bundled build were both tried') all scope the evidence precisely to the overhead test. required_elements_for_full_match is the single disjunctive 'mentions_reserving_vram_or_reducing_gpu_layers', so nothing is graded on an untested num_gpu result. At most this is an optional comment-wording enrichment, not a defect.

Remaining issues are fidelity-level, not scoring-inverting: e4 bundles two distinct handler turns (find-fix request and the handler-supplied beta build) into one info_id, the e5 keyword set leans on release-management specifics, and the root-cause condition drags in an unrelated DXVA/D3D11 detail.
bmo_1865928.strengths: The #1 failure mode is avoided: the only blind edge (e6, the three other NV12 prefs) is a genuine falsified attempt — c56 'I also tried FF 120.0 with the following settings, but they have no effect ... layers.iosurfaceimage.use-nv12=false / media.wmf.use-nv12-format=false / media.wmf.zero-copy-nv12-textures=false' — and the working pref (gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win) is correctly NOT marked blind. Measurement-class handling is exemplary: the mozregression window (c18), the pref-flip confirmation (c30/c31, which doubles as a workaround) and the test-build run are all clarification_only, and their user_answers stay at the evidence level while the engineer-side condensation (pushlog 431b4ea6..52459518 derived by participant5 in c21, mapping to bug 1857385) is correctly parked in inference_hint. The Task body contains only c0-c4 content with no diagnosis or pref names. All image bindings are correct (att9364836/9364837 opening hwa-on/off, att9365718 the reporter's regression progress, att9365725 the stats-for-nerds shot answering c16's codec question, att9365938/9365956 the two find-fix progress shots), and participant6's look-alike attachments are deliberately not reused. The multi-user merge (participant6) is confined to e6 and declared in its comment. persona_hint matches the reporter exactly, including c52's 'is there a way to install/test this on Windows w/o hosing my normal FF install and profiles'. satisfaction_conditions correctly separate symptom relief from verified resolution and explicitly forbid the falsified prefs and permanent HWA disablement.

Separately and much later, c50 (participant7): 'Below is a test build of Beta with bug 1865426 included. Can you please try it out' -> c52 reporter asks how to run it without hosing his profile -> c53 'Checked the version: 121.0b5 ... The video displayed correctly.' Two distinct assistant turns with different requested actions, ~20 comments apart, with an intervening unrelated request (c49 participant9 'check ... with latest nightly'). The graph's e4 collapses them into a single clarification whose two question_patterns are ALTERNATIVES ('Could you run a mozregression --find-fix...' / 'Here is a Beta test build containing the NV12 support check...'), so matching the first pattern still returns a user_answer that reports on 'the provided 121.0b5 test build' — a build the agent never supplied. That is an incoherent/leaking reveal, and worse, it hands over the post-fix verification that satisfaction_condition #5 explicitly demands ('Must have the reporter verify the fix ... before treating the issue as resolved') before any fix has been proposed. Note the graph splits the analogous pref-toggle measurement onto its own edge (e3), so the merge here is not a consistent modeling convention. refuted_claims.claim: [wrong_root_cause / low] at satisfaction_conditions[0]: The required root cause statement folds in 'D3D11 decoder device creation fails' as part of the causal mechanism, but the thread establishes hardware decoding was not in use at all, so the DXVA failure is a bystander symptom of the old GPU, not the source of the green frames.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The condition actually reads: 'Firefox 120 enabled YUV->NV12 conversion (gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win) on hardware whose GPU/driver path lacks NV12 support (older AMD, D3D11 decoder device creation fails), producing green frames.' The causal clause is precisely what the thread concludes — c48 (participant9): 'the GPU might not support NV12 ... NV12 support check was added by Bug 1865426', and c58 (participant7): 'originally caused by bug 1857385, which set the gfx.video.convert-yuv-to-nv12.image-host-win preference to true for Release builds.' The 'D3D11 decoder device creation fails' text sits inside a parenthetical that qualifies the HARDWARE ('older AMD, ...'), i.e. it characterizes the GPU/driver path, and does not assert that the DXVA failure produces the green frames. That is exactly the role the reviewer's own proposed fix assigns it ('keep the DXVA/AMDPreUVD4 line as supporting evidence of the old-GPU path'). The DXVA line is also genuine, quoted evidence from c16 and is one of the flags the reporter surfaced, so requiring it as corroboration is legitimate. The proposed rewrite is a stylistic sharpening, not a correction of a wrong root cause.

bmo_1913022.summary: The case tests whether an agent resists two brush-off dismissals (duplicate-closure and "install a third-party extension") and instead establishes that an intentional IDN-rework cleanup removed the network.IDN_show_punycode code path, then argues for restoring the pref and asks the user to verify on a build that actually contains the patch. The graph is a faithful and well-shaped encoding: both blind paths are genuinely falsified in the thread, the root cause matches c6 and c16 plus the bug's regressed_by metadata, the bisection is correctly modeled as a clarification carrying only raw output, and release/uplift logistics are kept out of the scored elements. Two fidelity problems remain: the root-cause id sits inside the user's info_state from N2 onward (the leak-repaired exemplar keeps such ids out of node info_state), and the regression-window answer invents a mozregression run by a reporter who never did one. Neither inverts scoring, but both should be repaired before the case is used.
bmo_1913022.strengths: Both blind paths are correctly labeled and precisely grounded: e1 (close as duplicate of bug 1332714) matches c4/c9 and was rejected by the reporter in c7/c8 and reopened; e3 (third-party punycode extension + duplicate of 1912865) matches c13 and was falsified in c15 ("This extension doesn't work... works only for few domains") and c2 (cannot install extensions on Android). No accepted approach is tagged blind. The root cause is exactly right and matches the metadata (regressed_by 1889536, see_also 1911935) and c6, and the fix mechanism in e5 mirrors c16 verbatim in substance ("Making `isLabelSafe` return early on a pref-bound atomic bool check"). The measurement-class rule is handled well: the regression window is a clarification_only edge whose answer carries only the raw pushlog URL plus "I have no idea which change in there matters", with the culprit reading pushed to info_inferred_by_engineer. Denoise is respected — uplift/graft/cadence chatter (c25, c30, c33, c35, c39, c40, c45) stays out of approach_keywords and required_elements, appearing only in concrete_example, and satisfaction condition 3 explicitly declares cadence a non-scored courtesy. The Task body draws only on c0-c3, all of which precede the first outside engagement at c4 (08:53:01), and contains no diagnosis or fix. required_info is fully gettable on the canonical path (regression window via e2, Android reliance via e4). persona_hint is accurate down to the premature verification (c27-c31, tested 131.0a1 hours after the 13:34 landing) and the later apology (c34). opening_images correctly points at attachment 9419021, the gif posted with c0.

refuted_claims.claim: [future_knowledge_leak / medium] at graph.nodes.N2.info_state / N3_x / N4 / N_terminal — id "pref_removal_was_intentional_cleanup_of_idn_rework": the root-cause conclusion is carried in the user-side info_state of every canonical node from N2 onward, even though it is engineer-side knowledge; fix = remove it from those info_states, keep only in info_inferred_by_engineer of e3/e5 per the bmo_1822845 convention.
refuted_claims.why_refuted: The provenance half of the claim is right (c6/participant3 is the source; the reporter clearly does not hold it — c7/c8/c11), but the encoding is exactly what the contract prescribes, and the stated leak mechanism does not exist. (a) Spec, prompts.py rule 3, verbatim: 'The destination may additionally gain engineer-inferred ids (also list them in info_inferred_by_engineer where a solution relies on them).' Rule 1 lists 'a solution's info_inferred_by_engineer' as a legitimate INTRODUCTION source for an id appearing in a node's info_state. The graph does precisely this: the id enters at e2's destination N2 and is declared in info_inferred_by_engineer on e3 and e5, the two solutions that rely on it. (b) The machine validator agrees: oncall_graph/models.py:195-253 accepts info_inferred_by_engineer as an introduction source for info_state (orphan-info check) and satisfies a solution's required_info from 'from-node info_state OR info_inferred_by_engineer'. The only hard prohibition (models.py:220) is the same id in BOTH required_info and info_inferred_by_engineer — this id is in no required_info anywhere, so that rule is not tripped. (c) The cited leak mechanism is false. speaker.py:219 does put info_state into the render context dict, but neither SPEAKER_REACT_PROMPT nor SPEAKER_PERSONA_PROMPT (user_simulator/prompts.py) has an info_state placeholder — the prompts are built from persona, symptoms_visible, history, intent and the offline draft only (speaker.py:141-171). Nothing in info_state reaches the LLM's context window. Speech comes from clarification user_answer text, volunteered_info and symptoms; this id is in no volunteered_info and no clarification, so the simulated user can never utter it. Its only runtime effect (responder.py:_advance_cascade) is to enter gathered_info_ids as grounding, which is the intended engineer-inference grant and is scoring-neutral here. (d) The bmo_1822845 comparison shows a difference, not a rule: there the root cause is never surfaced at any node, so it had nowhere else to live; rule 3 explicitly licenses the other placement.

(a) Rule 9 mandates folding all non-handler participants into ONE simulated user side, and the e2 comment declares the merge as required ('volunteer triager supplied the window') — so the user side genuinely did produce the pushlog. (b) Rule 4b then FORCES first-person rendering: 'every user_answer_in_this_oncall is in the reporter's own FIRST-PERSON voice — words they actually typed or could type. Never third-person narration ("the reporter provided...", "a second user ran...")'. The reviewer's proposed rewrite ('Someone on the bug posted a regression window for me') reintroduces exactly the third-party narration 4b discourages, so it is not clearly an improvement. (c) The persona-conflict argument is wrong on its own evidence: persona_hint says 'can edit about:config by following guides', so following a guide is in-persona rather than against it. (d) The load-bearing content — the exact c5 pushlog URL, raw, plus 'I have no idea which change in there matters' — is faithful and is textbook rule 4 (raw output, culprit not named), so there is no answer-key leak and no scoring effect. Residual: the clause 'guide someone linked me' is embroidery with no source event; a curator who wants tighter fidelity could trim it to 'I bisected with the pref set to true and got this pushlog', but that is cosmetic, not medium-severity fidelity damage.

gh_duckdb_duckdb_6937.summary: The case tests a long, evidence-heavy upstream performance thread: DuckDB 0.7.1 writes VARCHAR Parquet slowly, a current master build plus preserve_insertion_order=false gives a large speedup, the experimental parallel CSV reader silently drops rows on gzip input (30,559,373 vs 212,363,079), PR 6977 fixes the row loss but leaves unreadable Parquet, and #7253 (high memory / OOM) finally produces a fast, correct one-pass conversion verified by the reporter. The graph is unusually faithful: node/system-state boundaries, measurement-class edges, the blind PR-6977 attempt, all numbers, and the terminal verification all match the thread. The defects found are fidelity gaps, not scoring inversions: the last handler clarification round (c40: table-first control, parallel=False control, dataset sharing) is dropped, N4_x's symptom overgeneralizes a compressed-only failure, and one satisfaction condition mandates a query form the verified terminal run did not use.
gh_duckdb_duckdb_6937.strengths: Node/system-state modeling is correct: S1 (0.7.1) → S2 (dev1322, held constant across the three measurement rounds N1/N2/N3) → S3 (PR 6977 build) → S4 (dev2675). Every number in the clarification answers is verbatim-faithful: 549.536 vs 551.849 s and identical 4,794,409,184-byte outputs (c9), 31.687 s / 30,559,373 rows (c19), 254.119 s / 212,363,079 rows (c20), 168.212 s uncompressed control (c23), 588MB–681MB broken vs 4.14–4.82GB complete (c28/c30), 177 s and 212,363,079 verified (c43). The measurement-class rule is applied correctly and explicitly declared in e2's comment: experimental_parallel_csv and preserve_insertion_order toggles, which double as performance workarounds, are modeled as clarification edges (matching c10's handler-initiated suggestion), and the conclusions ('the gzip parallel path drops data', 'the reader partitioning is at fault') are kept out of the user's voice and placed in info_inferred_by_engineer. The is_known_blind_path=true on e4 is correct rather than the usual #1 defect: PR 6977 was genuinely tried and genuinely did not resolve the reporter's workload (c38 magic-bytes error), it lands on a proper *_x aftermath node with post-attempt symptoms, and there is still a forward path to the terminal — and satisfaction_conditions[2]/[3] correctly forbid treating experimental_parallel_csv on dev1322 or PR 6977 alone as the answer. The Task body is clean of all later knowledge. Image assignment is right on every attachment: img0 (the annotated COPY railroad diagram, 'where do I specify that the original CSV file as all_varchar?') sits on the select-node clarification, img1 (the 16-run matrix) on the benchmark clarification, img2/img3 on the post-6977 aftermath, img4 on the terminal. Terminal semantics are proper — user_perceives_resolved only after read_parquet returns the full count, and satisfaction_conditions[5] demands that verification. persona_hint matches the reporter's actual behaviour (Ruby benchmark generator in c26, compiled from source in c43). participant1's parallel benchmarking on their own machine (c1–c7) was correctly left out of the single simulated user side rather than silently merged.
